title: Related Rates II
subtitle: Harder geometry and harder reading: cones, shadows, angles and moving cars.

questions.text: Substituting $r = frac{h}{2}$ **before** differentiating is fine, because it is true at every moment.
questions.hint: Is the water’s radius half its depth the whole time, or only at one instant?
questions.explain: A relationship that always holds can go in before you differentiate.

questions.text: Substituting $h$ = 12 **before** differentiating is fine, because the problem asks about that moment.
questions.hint: What is the derivative of the constant 12?
questions.explain: $h$ = 12 is true at one instant only. Put it in early and $h$ becomes a constant, so its rate disappears.

questions.text: A kite flies 100 ft above the ground, $x$ ft away horizontally. Which equation links the angle of elevation $theta$ to $x$?
questions.hint: The height is opposite the angle and $x$ is adjacent.

questions.text: A 13-ft ladder slides down a wall. Which quantity is a **constant**?
options: The distance of the bottom from the wall
questions.hint: What does not change as the ladder slides?
questions.explain: The ladder stays 13 ft long, so 13 goes into the equation as a number: $x^2 + y^2 = 169$.

questions.text: A snowball melts so that its surface area decreases at 1 cm²/min. In symbols:
questions.hint: Which quantity is the 1 cm²/min about?
questions.explain: The rate is about the surface area, and it is going down.

questions.text: Two cars leave an intersection, one heading east ($x$) and one north ($y$). $z$ is the distance between them. Which equation links them?
questions.hint: East and north make a right angle.
questions.explain: A right triangle: the Pythagorean theorem.

questions.text: In a problem about a changing angle, $frac{d theta}{dt}$ comes out in…
questions.hint: The derivative formulas for sine, cosine and tangent assume one kind of angle measure.
questions.explain: The trig derivative rules only work in radians, so the rate is in radians per second (or minute, or hour).

slides.text:
Water drains from a cone-shaped funnel 20 ft tall with top radius 10 ft. The water is $h$ ft deep and its surface has radius $r$.
$$V = frac{1}{3}pi r^2 h$$
We know $frac{dV}{dt}$ and want $frac{dh}{dt}$. What is in the way?
options: The formula has a second changing variable, $r$, and we do not know $frac{dr}{dt}$
The volume formula is wrong for water
slides.hint: Count the letters on the right side that change as the water drains.
slides.explain: Two changing variables would need two rates. The fix: get rid of $r$ before differentiating.

slides.text: Now the reading. “Water **drains** at 0.3 ft³/s.” What does that say?
slides.hint: Is the volume going up or down?
slides.explain: Draining means the volume goes down, so its rate is negative. Drains, shrinks, melts and slides down all mean a negative rate.
